200.title: Polish government sets out draft 2027 budget with deficit remaining at 7.1% of GDP
200.summary: Polish government sets out draft 2027 budget with deficit remaining at 7.1% of GDP Aug 28, 2026 | Business , Energy & Climate , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Revenues are projected to rise by 68.4 billion zloty to 695 billion zloty, leaving a nominal budget deficit of 282.6 billion zloty, the highest on record and 10 billion zloty more than this year.
200.body: Polish government sets out draft 2027 budget with deficit remaining at 7.1% of GDP Aug 28, 2026 | Business , Energy & Climate , Politics Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! The deficit is forecast at 7.1% of GDP, unchanged from 2026 but well above the level of 3.7% the government had committed to reach by 2027 after Poland was placed under the European Union’s excessive deficit procedure in 2024. Revenues are projected to rise by 68.4 billion zloty to 695 billion zloty, leaving a nominal budget deficit of 282.6 billion zloty, the highest on record and 10 billion zloty more than this year. Poland’s gross borrowing needs are projected at 565 billion zloty in 2027, below the 688 billion zloty budgeted for this year.

400.title: Europe heads into winter with gas storage at 20-year seasonal low
400.summary: As the Iran war has severely disrupted Qatari LNG supplies to Europe, sent gas and LNG prices in Europe and Asia skyrocketing, and heightened competition for the shrunk pool of readily available global LNG cargoes, Europe is heading for the 2026-2027 winter with one of its lowest levels of gas in storage in the past two decades, according to a report by OilPrice.com.
400.body: As the Iran war has severely disrupted Qatari LNG supplies to Europe, sent gas and LNG prices in Europe and Asia skyrocketing, and heightened competition for the shrunk pool of readily available global LNG cargoes, Europe is heading for the 2026-2027 winter with one of its lowest levels of gas in storage in the past two decades, according to a report by OilPrice.com. Europe’s gas storage is just 63 percent full, its lowest level for this time of the year in nearly two decades, according to data from Gas Infrastructure Europe. For instance, the European benchmark natural gas prices in Europe at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF) surged this August to the highest since 2023, and so did the LNG prices in northwest Europe. Energy analysts say, Europe faces a winter [2026/2027] with the highest prices for gas and electricity in four years, with even higher gas needs next year for the next winter, unless LNG starts flowing out of the Strait of Hormuz very soon.
